item.title: SNB decision: franc down, euro up
item.description: The SNB keeps the reference rate at 0%, bringing the euro above 0.94 francs and the dollar to annual highs.
item.content:encoded:
## In breve - Franco svizzero in calo dopo decisione tassi BNS - Euro risale sopra 0,94 franchi, dollaro ai massimi annuali - BNS mantiene tasso di riferimento allo 0% - Svalutazione in linea con differenziali tassi esteri
## Fatti chiave Tasso di riferimento: 0% Cambio Euro: 0,9423 franchi Cambio Dollaro: 0,8268 franchi Deprezzamento franco: circa 3% da giugno
La Banca nazionale svizzera (BNS) ha annunciato stamattina la sua decisione sui tassi d'interesse, innescando una reazione immediata sui mercati valutari. Il franco ha perso terreno in modo netto, mentre l'euro è risalito sopra la soglia di 0,94 franchi e il dollaro ha raggiunto il livello più alto da circa un anno rispetto alla valuta elvetica.
Attualmente, il dollaro viene scambiato a 0,8268 franchi, mentre l'euro si attesta a 0,9423 franchi. La decisione della BNS, che era stata prevista dai mercati, è stata quella di mantenere il tasso di riferimento allo zero per cento. Tuttavia, l'attenzione degli operatori si è spostata rapidamente dalle cifre dei tassi alle comunicazioni della banca centrale riguardanti la gestione del franco.
### Il monitoraggio della BNS Secondo un osservatore di mercato, la BNS sta ora monitorando con maggiore attenzione le fluttuazioni del tasso di cambio in entrambe le direzioni. Questo approccio è fondamentale perché un franco più forte potrebbe aiutare a contrastare le pressioni inflazionistiche che arrivano dall'estero, specialmente considerando il recente aumento dei prezzi dell'energia.
Il presidente della BNS, Martin Schlegel, ha precisato nel testo del discorso sulla decisione dei tassi di giovedì che la valuta nazionale si è deprezzata di circa il 3 percento su base ponderata per il commercio a partire da giugno. Questa svalutazione è considerata in linea con l'ampliamento dei differenziali dei tassi d'interesse tra la Svizzera e le principali aree valutarie. Sebbene i tassi a lungo termine in Svizzera siano leggermente aumentati, lo hanno fatto in misura meno marcata rispetto a quanto avvenuto all'estero, rendendo il franco relativamente meno attraente per gli investitori globali. ### Implications for the purchasing power of the frontier The weakening of the franc has a direct and immediate impact on the lives of those who work in Switzerland and reside in Italy. For a frontier worker, a more favourable exchange rate of the euro compared to the franc (i.e. a stronger euro) means that, with the same salary in francs, the amount converted into euros will be lower. This phenomenon concretely reduces the purchasing power for those who move their earnings across borders to cover expenses in euros.
Considering that the euro has risen above 0.94 francs, those who receive their salary in CHF and convert it daily or monthly into EUR will suffer a contraction in the real value of their income. This scenario is the opposite of what happened during periods of strong appreciation of the franc, where each franc earned was worth more euros.
### The effect on inflation and import costs The SNB highlighted how the devaluation of the franc is reflected in inflation. Compared to June, the institution revised its medium-term inflation forecasts upwards. This is because a weaker franc makes goods and services imported into Switzerland more expensive. For the frontier worker who makes purchases in Swiss territory, this could result in an increase in consumer prices.
According to the SNB's forecasts, inflation is expected to rise again slightly in the fourth quarter of 2026, before falling again in 2027.
## Useful tools to protect your net income To reduce FX leakage, compare [CHF-EUR exchange options](nav:exchange) and [banks for cross-border workers](nav:banks). ### How to manage exchange rate risk For cross-border workers, the exchange rate movement is one of the most volatile variables of the payroll. When the franc loses ground, as happened after the latest SNB decision, it is essential to constantly monitor the currency value to decide when to convert savings or pay current expenses. In a depreciation phase, it might be less convenient to immediately convert the entire salary into euros.
### Operational strategies for the cross-border worker For those who want to optimise financial management, the following steps can be followed:
1. Rate monitoring: Keep an eye on SNB communications and the movement of pairs like CHF/EUR to avoid conversions at peak negative moments. 2. Account diversification: Keep part of savings in Swiss francs to cover expenses incurred in Switzerland (such as health insurance or social security contributions) and convert into euros only what is strictly necessary for expenses in Italy. 3. Medium‑term planning: Consider that, according to the SNB, inflation could rise again in 2026, influencing the cost of imported goods.
### SNB intervention and outlook Martin Schlegel reiterated that the national bank remains ready to intervene in the foreign‑exchange market if necessary. This means that the franc's value is not left exclusively to the free market, but can be corrected by the SNB to support the Swiss economy, facilitating export‑oriented companies.
For those working in Ticino, the balance between a strong franc (which protects against imported inflation) and a weak franc (which favours export) creates uncertainty. item.title: LPP tax refund blocked for border workers
item.description: From 2024, the Canton of Ticino no longer reimburses the 7% tax at source on LPP capital, forcing border workers to also pay the 5% Italian substitute tax.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - Cantons no longer refund withholding tax on LPP capital - Issue originated in 2024 in Canton Ticino, now extended to other cantons - OCST brought the case before the Tax Law Chamber - Judgment expected likely during 2027
## Key facts - What: No refund of withholding tax on LPP capital - When: Issue started in 2024 - Where: Canton Ticino and other Swiss cantons - Who: Cross‑border workers residing in Italy - Swiss rate: 7% (average) - Italian rate: 5% (substitute) - Institutions involved: OCST, Tax Law Chamber of Canton Ticino
Canton Ticino introduced in 2024 an interpretative change affecting cross‑border workers who choose to receive their second‑pillar assets, i.e., the LPP, as a lump‑sum. The novelty is that cantonal tax authorities have stopped refunding the withholding tax deducted at the time of capital redemption for residents in Italy. This decision has not remained limited to Ticino, but has spread to other cantons, making the problem potentially relevant for all cross‑border workers.
### Tax authority's position According to the Ticino tax authority's interpretation, the 5% substitute tax applied in Italy would constitute a form of preferential taxation. For this reason, Canton Ticino believes that the provisions of the Italy‑Switzerland double‑taxation convention should not apply. That treaty states that pension benefits linked to a terminated employment are, in principle, taxable only in the beneficiary's state of residence. By denying the convention's applicability, Ticino has begun refusing requests for refund of the withheld tax.
OCST has strongly contested this interpretation from the start. To protect its members, the organisation has provided assistance in claim procedures and, in June 2026, formally brought the case before the Tax Law Chamber of Canton Ticino. The legal process is currently pending and a definitive decision is awaited to clarify the legitimacy of the levy. Parallel friendly procedures at the international level between Italy and Switzerland have been attempted but ended negatively. For cross‑border workers wishing to manage their pension savings, it is useful to monitor the [refunds](nav:ristorni) provided by current regulations. Current fiscal situation creates significant uncertainty for those planning the redemption of the LPP. To understand the economic impact, it is necessary to compare the previously consolidated mechanism with the new practice adopted by the Cantons. Previously, the system worked linearly: at the moment of redemption, Switzerland applied a withholding tax, on average 7%. The cross‑border worker then declared that capital in Italy, paying the substitute tax of 5%, and finally requested from Switzerland the refund of the initially withheld portion. This allowed avoiding double taxation, respecting the principle of taxation in the state of residence.\n\nExtension of the problem to the various Cantons\nA fundamental technical detail concerns the origin of the levy: the withholding tax on the LPP capital is not collected by the Canton where the worker performs the professional activity, but by the one where the pension fund is based. This means that a cross‑border worker who works permanently in Ticino could be insured with a pension fund headquartered in Zurich, Bern or Basel. Initially, the block of refunds concerned only those insured with funds based in Ticino. However, the alignment of the other Cantons to this new interpretation has dramatically amplified the scope of the problem, affecting anyone with a pension fund in any Swiss Canton that has adopted the same practice.\n\nHypothetical scenarios and fiscal risks\nIn a hypothetical scenario, a worker who redeems his capital today has to bear both levies: the Swiss withholding tax (average 7%) and the Italian substitute tax (5%). If in the past the Swiss tax was recovered, now that amount remains in the cantonal coffers. This results in a higher overall fiscal burden compared to the past, reducing the net amount actually received by the cross‑border worker. The complexity of the matter increases as friendly international procedures have not yielded positive results, leaving the legal case outcome as the only hope. Those who need to assess the impact of these withholdings on their assets can use a [calculator](nav:calculator) to estimate the fiscal costs.
## Useful tools for your case To verify your within/over 20 km tax scenario, use the [net salary calculator](nav:calculator) and the [tax return guide](nav:tax-return). For cross‑border workers who are facing this issue or who expect to cash out their LPP capital soon, the current strategy is to wait for the legal proceedings to evolve. The ruling of the Tax Law Chamber of the Canton of Ticino is the key element that will determine whether the tax authority's interpretation is correct. According to forecasts, the final decision is likely to arrive during 2027. Until then, uncertainty remains high and refund requests risk being systematically denied.
### Operational steps and complaint handling Those who have already had their withholding‑tax refund denied can follow these steps based on OCST activity: - Verify the location of your pension fund to identify which canton made the withholding. - Consider union or professional assistance to start formal complaint procedures. - Keep all documentation related to the capital redemption and communications with the Swiss tax administration. - Monitor updates regarding the appeal brought before the Tax Law Chamber, as the ruling will potentially affect many similar cases.
It is important to remember that the Italian 5% tax must still be paid to be compliant with the residence tax authority, regardless of whether Switzerland refunds the 7% share. Managing cross‑border pension requires constant attention, especially concerning the second pillar. Those who wish to explore how these variables affect their retirement planning should consult the guides on [pension](nav:pension) available on the portal.
For precise budget management and to understand how taxes affect net available income, we recommend using our salary‑tax calculator: [salary calculator](nav:calculator).

item.title: Living in Brenna and working in Ticino as a border worker
item.description: Comprehensive analysis on connections, taxation and costs for those who choose to reside in Brenna and work in Switzerland.
item.content:encoded:
## In a nutshell - Tax at source: withheld only in Switzerland. - New Agreement: in force from 1 January 2024. - Deductible for new frontier workers: 10,000 euros. - Double taxation agreement: 9 December 1976.
## Key facts - Frontier Agreement: 1 January 2024 - Deductible for new frontier workers: €10,000 - Exemption for old frontier workers: €7,500 - IT-CH Convention: 9 December 1976 - AVS/AI/IPG: 5.3% - LPP: 7-18%
Brenna is a border municipality that offers a strategic location for those who wish to work in Canton Ticino. The management of daily commuting is based on the use of the border crossing, facilitating access to the Ticino production centres. For those who move to Brenna, the tax aspect is decisive: the tax at source is withheld exclusively in Switzerland, while Italy avoids double taxation through the application of a tax credit in the EC framework of model 730.
### Updated tax legislation
The regulatory framework has been profoundly modified by the New Frontier Agreement, signed on 23 December 2020 and in force since 1 January 2024, ratified in Italy with Law 83 of 13 June 2023. This agreement distinguishes between old and new frontier workers. Old frontier workers, i.e. those who were already such before 17 July 2023, benefit from an exemption of 7,500 euros and a transitional regime that extends from 2024 to 2033. The new frontier workers, on the other hand, have a deductible of 10,000 euros.
The ## Practical analysis for the cross‑border worker
Choosing to live in Brenna and work in Ticino entails several practical implications. The first aspect is the cost of living, which varies significantly between Italy and Switzerland. A cross‑border worker residing in Brenna can optimise their savings thanks to the cost difference between the two countries.
### Calculation of net salary and social security contributions
To understand the real impact on net salary, it is essential to analyse Swiss social security contributions. The AVS/AI/IPG deductions amount to 5.3% borne by the employee. Unemployment insurance (AD/AC) is set at 1.1% with a maximum ceiling of CHF 148,200. Moreover, the LAINF (accident insurance) describes the LAINF rate between 0.7% and 1.5%.
Regarding occupational pension (LPP), contributions vary from 7% to 18% depending on the age band, starting from 25 years. This two‑pillar pension system is fundamental for the worker's long‑term financial planning. In Italy, IRPEF is applied with progressive rates: 23% up to €28,000, 35% between €28,001 and €50,000, and 43% above €50,000.
### Health management and insurance
A critical aspect is health insurance. LAMal is the mandatory health insurance, not a tax. Cross‑border workers with a G permit have an option right to choose between Swiss insurance or that of their country of residence. Deductibles for adults are set between CHF 300 and CHF 2,500. Health management is the final piece to complete the relocation planning to Brenna for those working in Ticino.

The Federal Council has responded to the written questions submitted by National Councillors Simone Gianini and Piero Marchesi regarding the traffic situation between Bellinzona and Locarno. The complaints from many motorists and cross-border commuters concerned the worsening of traffic conditions, characterized by increased queues and longer travel times. This situation emerged following the recent commissioning of the first traffic lights in Cadenazzo, which are part of the broader project by the Federal Roads Office aimed at equipping the entire route up to Quartino with traffic lights.

However, the executive reiterated that the traffic light system will be constantly monitored until the completion of the works scheduled for 2027. Only then, according to institutional estimates, will the effectiveness of the measure become clearly evident. In the meantime, this continuous monitoring should allow the infrastructure's response capacity to be adjusted to real road conditions, thereby progressively improving traffic flow along the road axis affected by the interventions. ### The motivations of Ustra and the road context Despite the initial inconvenience perceived by road users, the Federal Roads Office still considers it necessary to adopt immediate measures to improve traffic flow while waiting for the future A2-A13 motorway connection between Bellinzona and Locarno to be built. However, this strategic work runs the real risk of suffering a further postponement towards the 2050s, both due to the maturity of the project compared to other competing works and for financial reasons. Among the various points raised are the request for concrete data regarding queues and travel times compared to the previous period, the verification of a possible reassessment of traffic light synchronization, and the introduction of any countermeasures to facilitate fluidity during rush hours. ## Key facts What: Job cuts and business repositioning Who: Sunrise How many jobs: Up to 450 out of 2,900 Previous period: 147 layoffs in February Consultation start: October
A new wave of staff cuts is looming for Sunrise. On Monday, the operator announced a repositioning of its activities and the goal of substantial medium-term savings, with the prospect of eliminating up to 450 full-time jobs out of its current workforce of 2,900. According to a press release, the company plans a deep reorientation in order to anticipate emerging market and technological trends, and to permanently strengthen its execution capacity in operational activities as well as its market position. The savings in question have not been quantified for now. Regarding employment, a consultation procedure with union representatives will be launched in October. Employees working in retail stores and customer service should largely be spared from the cuts. Last February, Sunrise had already announced the dismissal of 147 people.
### Reactions and company climate The restructuring announcement immediately sparked reactions in the union world. The Syndicom union reacted on Monday afternoon by strongly condemning the measure. In the press release issued by the union, it is stated that the planned drastic job cuts at Sunrise are an affront to the staff. Syndicom defended the commitment of the employees, who have worked with great energy for years and contributed to the company's success, supporting numerous changes in recent years. The company now faces a delicate phase of confrontation with employee representatives to define the scope and methods of the reorganization announced at the beginning of the week, which involves hundreds of employees across the entire operational structure. ### The position of the Syndicom trade union The Syndicom trade union expressed a very critical stance regarding the corporate decision communicated by Sunrise. In statements released on Monday afternoon, the union organization emphasized how employees have demonstrated great energy in recent years and have actively contributed to the company's success, facing and supporting numerous structural changes. Faced with the prospect of eliminating up to 450 full-time jobs, the union demands that the consultation procedure be initiated quickly, so that the staff has sufficient time to present concrete alternative proposals. Syndicom also expects Sunrise to exploit all possibilities to preserve jobs and assume its social responsibilities, rather than unilaterally placing cost and performance objectives before the interests of the staff. ### Details on the scope of the restructuring The new wave of cuts announced by Sunrise follows a previous intervention last February, when the operator had already announced the dismissal of 147 people. The current plan involves a deep reorientation aimed at anticipating market and technological developments and strengthening execution capacity in operational activities and market position. However, the expected savings have not been quantified at this stage. item.title: Expensive fuel prices in Ticino: tax reduction request
item.description: Motion filed in Bern to lighten the tax burden on gasoline, diesel and heating oil in the face of historic hikes.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - Sharp rise in gasoline and diesel prices - Motion submitted by Lorenzo Quadri - Requested tax relief on fuels - Temporary measures against cost of living
## Key facts - Proponent: Lorenzo Quadri - Recipient: Federal Council - Price of 95-octane gasoline (end February 2026): 1.67 francs per litre - Price of 95-octane gasoline (17 September): 2.10 francs per litre - Record diesel price: 2.41 francs per litre - Mineral oil tax: about 4.4 billion francs per year - CO2 tax: 120 francs per tonne
Petroleum product prices continue to rise sharply, exerting strong pressure on citizens' purchasing power and on the entire Ticinese and Swiss economy. The situation has prompted Lega national councillor Lorenzo Quadri to submit a motion to the Federal Council requesting an immediate and temporary intervention to alleviate the tax burden weighing on fuels and heating oil. The legislative proposal follows a similar parliamentary act presented by Lega coordinator Daniele Piccaluga, who acted at cantonal level, asking the State Council to act on fiscal levers, such as increasing deductions for professional expenses. As highlighted in the text of the federal motion, the objective is to temporarily suspend the collection of at least part of the mineral oil tax destined for the Confederation's general coffers, of VAT and of a share of the CO2 tax applied to heating oil. This measure aims to mitigate the impact of the price increase for consumers, businesses and craftsmen, at a time when energy costs risk negatively affecting the whole economic chain.
### Price dynamics and fiscal revenue The seriousness of the economic situation is illustrated by the data on fuel price trends. 95-octane gasoline, which traded at an average of 1.67 francs per litre at the end of February 2026, reached 2.10 francs per litre on 17 September. The increase for diesel is even steeper, hitting a record price of 2.41 francs per litre. Faced with these rises, the document highlights the significant weight of current taxation: the mineral oil tax generates about 4.4 billion francs annually. Of this amount, 40% of the revenue from fuels flows directly into the Confederation's general coffers, while the remainder is allocated to financing transport and the Fostra fund. Precisely on the non‑earmarked component of fiscal revenue, according to the Ticino parliamentarian, the Confederation has sufficient leeway to intervene and grant temporary relief to taxpayers. The impact of energy price increases and the comparison with neighboring countries highlight the operational difficulties faced by Swiss distributors located in the border area. The motion submitted in Bern draws attention to the policies adopted by the governments of several European nations, including the states bordering Switzerland, which regularly apply discounts or reductions on fuel prices to support households and economic operators. This disparity in tax treatment puts Swiss operators in the border region at a clear disadvantage, forced to compete with foreign competitors strongly favored by lighter tax regimes. To delve deeper into the overall economic impact of daily expenses and the cost of living, you can consult the available analysis tools such as the [cost of living Ticino vs Italy](nav:cost-of-living) to assess real differences on the ground.
### The weight of heating oil and the CO2 tax Besides motor fuels, the request for tax relief advanced to the Federal Council also directly concerns the domestic and industrial heating sector. The CO2 tax levied on heating oil is currently set at 120 francs per tonne of emitted carbon dioxide, an amount corresponding to about 32 cents per litre of heating oil consumed. According to the motion's text, in an exceptional economic phase, the federal administration should temporarily waive part of these high tax revenues. The declared aim is to give financial breathing space not only to those obliged to use a car daily to get to work, but also to craft and commercial enterprises suffering from increased fixed operating costs. For those who face daily cross-border commuting and wish to plan their transport-related expenses precisely, it is useful to regularly check the options for calculating and managing transport costs via the [commuter car cost](nav:car-cost).

The institutional procedure initiated with the filing of the motion by Lorenzo Quadri now requires formal examination by the Federal Council, called upon to express its opinion on the sustainability and on the advisability of temporarily suspending tax levies on hydrocarbons. Meanwhile, workers and residents who suffer the combined burden of energy inflation and taxes need to closely monitor the evolution of the regulatory and fiscal framework at both the federal and cantonal levels. The proposals made at the local level, such as the increase in the possibilities of deducting professional expenses discussed at the cantonal level, represent an alternative channel of intervention that deserves to be closely followed by taxpayers to optimize their annual tax burden.

item.content:encoded:
## In brief - First day for the new Pharmacy course at Insubria - Lectures at the Polo scientifico in via Valleggio, Como - Forty-seven students attending - Local and Swiss pharmacies involved
## Key facts - Start date: September 22 - Main venue: Polo scientifico in Como - Number of students: 47 - Course duration: Five years - Degree class: LM-13
The first lecture of the new single-cycle master's degree course in Pharmacy at the University of Insubria took place on Tuesday, September 22, in lecture hall VA2 of the Polo scientifico in via Valleggio, Como, starting with forty-seven students in the classroom. The new class was welcomed by the Deputy Rector of the University of Insubria Umberto Piarulli, the Director of the Department of Science and High Technology Michela Prest, and the course coordinator, Professor Simona Galli, who addressed the students with a welcome greeting and introduced the educational path that will accompany them over the next five years. Also present were Professor Luca Nardo, who held the first lecture of the course, and researchers Orlando Santoro and Nicolò Baranzini. Professors Tiziana Rubino and Marina Protasoni, both course lecturers, also spoke via video link from Varese. Deputy Rector Umberto Piarulli explained that the course was built by listening to the local community, pharmacies, and the pharmaceutical industry, with the aim of offering a useful and innovative path, wishing the students to approach it with passion, commitment, and dialogue. Professor Michela Prest shared that the creation of this course was a completely new and highly engaging experience, allowing her to get to know the world of pharmacy up close and the many professionals revolving around it, from community pharmacies to industry, from communication to research. Professor Simona Galli drew attention to the transition from school to university, emphasizing that the study method changes profoundly and requires autonomy, organization, and responsibility in time management.
### Course structure and locations
The course belongs to the LM-13 class for Pharmacy and Industrial Pharmacy, has open access, and lasts five years. The qualification enables the exercise of the profession of pharmacist pursuant to Interministerial Decree 635/2022. The curriculum was jointly designed by the Department of Science and High Technology, directed by Michela Prest, and the Department of Biotechnology and Life Sciences, directed by Flavia Marinelli. The main location is the Polo scientifico in Como, where frontal lectures and practical laboratory activities in the chemical and pharmacological fields take place. Laboratory activities in the biological area will also be organized at the Busto Arsizio university campus, coordinated by Professor Tiziana Rubino. The curriculum integrates lectures and practical exercises and provides skills in the chemical, biological, biochemical, biomedical, pharmaceutical, pharmacological, toxicological, legislative, and deontological sectors. The goal is to train professionals capable of addressing the evolution of the pharmacist's role, which is increasingly integrated into the health system and a point of reference for citizens and health professionals, as well as being a drug expert. Training also looks at career opportunities in pharmaceutical industries, public entities, research institutes, and regulatory bodies, with skills ranging from research and development to production, from quality control to drug dispensing and pharmacovigilance. ### Advanced skills and artificial intelligence
Particular attention is also dedicated to the applications of artificial intelligence in clinical project management, resource allocation, pharmacovigilance, and drug development, with the aim of providing tools capable of supporting data-driven decisions. The new course relies on qualified faculty, laboratories, and national and international scientific collaborations. Industry stakeholders also contributed to its design, including Orders of Pharmacists, Federfarma, representatives of specialization schools and PhD programs, and pharmaceutical companies, who are called upon to maintain an active role in the educational path. This network of collaborations allows students to acquire training that directly responds to the current needs of the job market, taking into account the technological and scientific transformations underway in the healthcare sector.
### Cross-border integration and practical internships
A key element for the region is the involvement of pharmacies in the local area and nearby Switzerland, which will offer students internship opportunities and direct engagement with the professional reality. This opportunity allows future pharmacists to experience different healthcare systems and broaden their career prospects in a particularly dynamic border geographic context. For those looking at job opportunities in the Insubric area, having access to educational practical experiences that include the Swiss reality represents a significant added value in building their professional profile. Collaborations with Swiss facilities offer a privileged window into the operating procedures, regulations, and management specifics of cross-border pharmacies, preparing graduates to navigate competently in a broad and integrated job market. To learn more about professional opportunities and employment integration methods in the region, you can consult the dedicated section on [job offers](nav:jobs).

The course of study requires a strong commitment right from the first months, as highlighted by the professors during the first lecture. To best cope with the transition from high school to university, the University provides tutoring and continuous support tools. Constant dialogue between students and faculty represents the fundamental pillar for overcoming difficulties and successfully managing the five-year study load. Free access to the course allows all interested parties who meet the requirements to enroll and embark on this highly qualifying educational path, which combines traditional pharmacy skills with the new frontiers of scientific research, technology, and digital health data management.
### Career prospects and employment opportunities
The training offered by the University of Insubria opens up multiple career paths, not limited solely to the management of the community pharmacy. Graduates will be able to aim for prominent roles in pharmaceutical industries, public bodies, research institutes, and regulatory agencies, operating in the sectors of production, quality control, and pharmacovigilance. item.title: Living in Bregnano and working in Ticino: a practical guide for border workers
item.description: Travel times, costs, taxes and procedures: everything border workers from Bregnano need to know before accepting a job in Ticino.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - Average commuting time Bregnano-Chiasso: **45-60 minutes** (traffic permitting) - Cost of living in Ticino 20-30% higher than in Bregnano (e.g. Lugano rent: +28% vs Como) - New cross-border worker tax regime active since 1 January 2024 (Italy-Switzerland Agreement 2020) - Tax exemption: €10,000 for new cross-border workers (employment started after 17/07/2023)
## Key facts Distance: 25 km Bregnano-Chiasso Main border crossings: Brogeda (A9), Ponte Chiasso (SS340), Fornasette (secondary) Travel time: 45-60 min (car), up to 90 min during rush hour Cost of living: +20-30% Ticino vs Lombardy (e.g. monthly shopping: CHF 450 vs €300 per household) Withholding tax: 5.3% AVS/AI + 1.1% AD (income up to CHF 148,200) Tax exemption: €10,000 (new cross-border workers)
The route from Bregnano to Chiasso, the main gateway to Canton Ticino, covers approximately 25 km. By car via the A9 motorway and the Brogeda crossing, it takes 45-60 minutes with smooth traffic. However, queues at crossings (especially Brogeda and Ponte Chiasso) and congestion during commuting hours (6:30-9:00 and 17:00-19:00) can extend travel times to 90 minutes. A commuter leaving Bregnano at 6:30 a.m. averages 50 minutes, while at 7:30 a.m. the time increases to 75 minutes. The rail alternative (S11 Como-Chiasso line) involves a change at Como San Giovanni and similar duration (65-80 minutes), with a monthly integrated TILO-Trenord pass at CHF 180 for the Italian-Swiss section. For those working in Lugano (30 km from Bregnano), travel time increases to 70-90 minutes by car, with tolls of CHF 40/month for the A9.
From a tax perspective, cross-border workers are subject to withholding tax in Switzerland. The new Italy-Switzerland Agreement, signed on 23 December 2020 and effective since 1 January 2024, introduces a €10,000 exemption for new cross-border workers (employment started after 17 July 2023). A worker with an annual gross income of CHF 80,000 (approx. €76,000) pays Swiss taxes of CHF 5,840 (7.3%), but benefits from the exemption: actual taxation on CHF 63,200. Pre-existing cross-border workers retain the exemption up to €7,500 until 2033. Withholding tax includes AVS/AI contributions (5.3%), AD (1.1% up to CHF 148,200), and possible costs for LAINF (0.7%) and LPP (variable).
> 'The €10,000 exemption mitigates the tax impact for new entrants, but requires attention to double taxation' (Dr. Rossi, cross-border tax expert).
Operational checklist: 1. Request G permit from Swiss employer within 8 days of hiring 2. Register with AIRE within 90 days of relocation 3. Choose health insurance: Swiss Health Insurance Fund (average cost CHF 350/month) or Italian (ENI agreement) 4. Report foreign income to Italian Tax Authority (Quadro OE, mod. Redditi)
Scenario comparison: - New cross-border worker (2024): Income CHF 70,000 → CH tax: CHF 3,900 (5.6%) after exemption - Pre-2023 cross-border worker: Same income → CH tax: CHF 4,600 (6.6%) with €7,500 exemption - Annual transport cost: Car (fuel+tolls): €2,800 vs Train: €2,200 (pass)
⚠️ Warning: From 2025, minor crossings like Fornasette may require digital permits for access during commuting hours. Check updates at www.ti.ch/frontalieri. ## Cost of Living: Practical Comparison The cost of living in Ticino exceeds the Bregnano area by 25-35%, with peaks in rents: in Lugano, a studio apartment starts at CHF 1,500 (vs. €650 in Como city). A two-room apartment in Mendrisio costs CHF 1,800, compared to €800 in Olgiate Comasco. Food expenses show surcharges of 18-22%: a liter of milk costs CHF 1.80 (Coop Ticino) vs. €1.20 (Conad Lombardia), while a kilogram of Barilla pasta reaches CHF 2.50 vs. €1.50. Fuel (gasoline 95) stands at CHF 1.82/liter (2024 average) vs. €1.75 in Italy, but Swiss diesel (CHF 1.75) is more convenient. According to the Federal Statistical Office (2023), household utilities cost 30% more: electricity at CHF 0.28/kWh vs. €0.22 in Lombardy.
## Commuting: Options and Costs Private car commuting entails monthly costs of CHF 350-450: fuel (CHF 200 for 1,200 km), highway vignette (CHF 40/year), parking (CHF 150-250/month in Lugano). Italian tolls (A9 Como-Chiasso: €5 per leg) add €200/month for 20 working days. Public transport offers the Arcobaleno pass (zones 10-20-Mi1): CHF 285/month for Chiasso-Lugano-Como, with TILO trains every 30 minutes (6:00-22:00). The new X30 bus line (Chiasso-Lugano, 45 minutes) costs CHF 7.60 per ride. Average travel times: 50 minutes by car vs. 70 minutes by train from Como to Lugano.
## Recommended Residential Areas To balance costs and travel times, many cross-border workers choose border municipalities in Ticino: in Morbio Inferiore (15 minutes from Chiasso), a two-room apartment costs CHF 1,250-1,400, while in Balerna (with train station) solutions are available at CHF 1,350. In Italy, areas near the A9 (Rovellasca, Lurate Caccivio) offer rentals at €700-850 for three-room apartments, with a 30-minute drive to Melano (CH). Note regulatory requirements: from 2025, Ticino residents for >90 days must take out Swiss health insurance (approx. CHF 380/month).
> 'Saving on fuel in Italy is worthwhile, but time lost in traffic is significant' (Marco R., cross-border worker since 2018).
Operational Checklist: - 📊 Calculate net cost: gross CH salary - withholding tax (average rate 15-18%) - commuting costs (deductible up to CHF 3,600/year). - 💡 Verify customs requirements: declaration of assets >CHF 5,000 and ban on importing meat/milk from the EU. - ⚠️ Update documents: G permit (cross-border workers) with annual renewal and certificate of origin for Italy-registered vehicles.
## Useful planning tools To estimate your pension strategy, use the [pension planner](nav:pension) and the [pillar 3 simulator](nav:pillar3). ## What to Consider Before Relocating ### Tax Aspects: Double Taxation Swiss withholding tax (currently 10.25% in Ticino for 2023) applies exclusively to employment income earned in the canton. Italian-sourced income such as rents (e.g., €12,000 annual from a Milan apartment) or dividends must be declared in Italy via the **quadro CE** of the 730 form, leveraging tax credits to prevent double taxation under the 2015 Italy-Switzerland agreement. New cross-border workers have 30 days from employment start to register with the Italian Revenue Agency (AA9/12 form).
### Health Insurance (LAMal) Within 3 months of hiring, cross-border workers must obtain basic LAMal-compliant insurance in Switzerland. In 2023, average Ticino premiums range from CHF 350 (Helsana, CHF 2,500 deductible) to CHF 480 (CSS, CHF 300 deductible) monthly per adult. Insurer choice (e.g., Groupe Mutuel, Concordia) impacts costs: a 40-year-old in Lugano typically pays CHF 420/month with standard deductible. ⚠️ Failure to enroll on time incurs fines up to CHF 5,000.
### Social Security: AVS and LPP Mandatory contributions deducted from Swiss paychecks include: - AVS/AI: 5.3% of salary (max CHF 49,290 annually in 2023) - AD/AC: 1.1% (up to CHF 147,840 only) - LPP: Mandatory from age 25. A 35-year-old earning CHF 80,000 contributes 7% (CHF 5,600 annually), with employers adding at least 50%. Vested funds are transferable only after 5 years.
💡 Concrete Actions: 1. Calculate net monthly pay using the [cross-border salary calculator](nav:calculator) (e.g., CHF 6,500 gross → CHF 4,800 net after taxes/LAMal) 2. Compare housing costs: average Lugano 2-bedroom (CHF 1,800/month) vs. Bregnano (€800/month) 3. Check commute times: Bregnano to Mendrisio (25 km) → 45-minute drive (2022 average) vs. 60-minute train
> '68% of cross-border workers underestimate commuting costs in their first year' (Ticino Statistical Office, 2022)
Before accepting an offer, simulate your monthly budget: - Commuting: TILO train pass (CHF 250/month) vs. car (CHF 400/month fuel/tolls) - Housing: Save €1,000/month living in Lombardy, but spend +CHF 300 on gas - Real net: CHF 7,000 salary → after withholding tax (CHF 735), LAMal (CHF 420), and LPP (CHF 385) → CHF 4,460 available Use tools like the [tax calculator](nav:calculator) to quantify purchasing power, factoring in Ticino inflation (+2.8% in 2023).

item.title: Castiglione Olona & Ticino: Guide for Border Workers
item.description: Travel times, taxation, cost of living and transfer advice: everything border crossers need to know before choosing Castiglione Olona as an Italian base.
item.content:encoded:
## In a nutshell - **Distance**: ~50 km from Castiglione Olona to the Brogeda border - Average travel time: 45-70 minutes by car (variable traffic on A9/A2) - Taxation: Swiss source tax (5-13%) + Italian tax credit - Cost of living: Ticino +30-40% vs Northern Italy, but average salaries +50% - Key advantage: Italian tax exemption up to €10,000 (new cross-border commuters)
## Key facts Border distance: 50 km Travel time: 45-70 min Tax exemption: €10,000 (new cross-border commuters) AVS rate: 5.3% Cost of living Ticino vs IT: +30-40% Cross-border agreement: In force since January 1, 2024
Castiglione Olona, with its historic center and efficient services, increasingly attracts cross-border commuters working in Ticino. Located approximately 50 km from the Brogeda border crossing, it represents a compromise between Italian quality of life and Swiss job opportunities. Travel times by car vary between 45 and 70 minutes, depending on traffic on the A9 and A2, while rail connections via Varese take about 90 minutes. Its strategic position near the A8/A9 motorway makes it preferable to more distant municipalities like Induno Olona or Ponte Tresa.
### Taxation: how the source tax works Cross-border commuters are subject to source tax in Switzerland (rates between 5% and 13% depending on canton and income), while in Italy they benefit from a tax credit that avoids double taxation. The new cross-border agreement that came into force on January 1, 2024 introduced a €10,000 exemption for new cross-border commuters (compared to €7,500 for those already active before July 17, 2023). Mandatory Swiss social contributions: AVS/AI/IPG (5.3%), AD/AC (1.1%), LAINF (0.7-1.5%) and LPP (7-18%).
### Cost of living: practical comparison Living in Castiglione Olona costs on average 30-40% less than in Ticino for rents, groceries and services. However, Ticino salaries are higher: a specialized worker earns around CHF 4,500 net per month, compared to €2,500 in Lombardy. Savings also come from the Italian tax exemption, which for an annual income of CHF 60,000 means €6,000 not taxed in Italy. However, watch out for hidden costs: Swiss car insurance (CHF 1,200/year), motorway vignette (CHF 40) and Italian tolls. ## Advantages and Disadvantages of Transferring **Benefits**: - Tax savings: Up to €10,000 tax-free in Italy for new frontier workers - Higher salaries: Average +50% compared to Northern Italy - Efficient services: Ticino health and transport accessible with G permit
Disadvantages: - Stressful commuting: Queues in Brogeda/Gaggiolo at rush hour - High car costs: CH insurance + maintenance for mountain routes - Mandatory LAMal: Swiss Health Insurance (CHF 300-2.500/anno)
### Recommended areas in Castiglione Olona Residential areas near the motorway exit (e.g. Via XXV Aprile) reduce access times to the A9. For families, the Villa Toledo area offers schools and parks. Avoid secondary roads to Vedano Olona if you depend on the car: in case of snow, the priority of evacuation is for the main arteries.
### Practical scenarios: what if… ...become a teleworker? The new agreement allows up to 90 days/year of working from home without tax impact. In addition, you risk losing the Italian franchise. ...exceed €50,000 per year? The Italian personal income tax rate is charged at 43% on the surplus part, but the tax credit mitigates the burden. ...I have an accident in Switzerland? The LAINF covers the costs, but it is worth supplementing with private insurance for non-occupational accidents.

## Useful planning tools To estimate your pension strategy, use the [pension planner](nav:pension) and the [pillar 3 simulator](nav:pillar3). ## Concrete Actions for Relocation ### Step 1: Obtain Permit G Apply online via the Canton Ticino portal within 8 days of employment. Required documents: employment contract, passport, proof of Italian residence. Cost: CHF 100 (annual renewal).
### Step 2: Choose Health Insurance Cross-border workers have the right to choose: within 3 months, select between: - **Swiss LAMal** (cost CHF 300–2,500/year depending on deductible) - Italian SSN (with E106 certificate, but note limitations for treatment in Switzerland)
### Step 3: Optimize Taxation Submit the 'Cross-border Workers' Declaration' to the Italian Revenue Agency by April 30 annually. Retain AVS contribution receipts for tax credits. For incomes over €50,000, evaluate the benefits of a deductible third-pillar 3a insurance policy in Switzerland.
### Essential Tools for Cross-Border Workers - [Net Salary Calculator](nav:calculator): Simulate tax and contribution impacts - [CHF/EUR Comparator](nav:exchange): Monitor exchange rates to optimize transfers - [Border Crossing Guide](nav:border-map): Real-time updates for Brogeda/Gaggiolo and alternative routes
📊 Typical Case: A cross-border worker earning CHF 72,000/year (CHF 6,000/month) pays source taxes of CHF 8,640 (12%), AVS contributions of CHF 3,816 (5.3%), and LAINF of CHF 540 (0.75%). In Italy, they receive a €6,000 tax credit on the exemption.
⚠️ Warning: From 2024, new cross-border workers lose the exemption if working more than 90 days/year from home. Always verify with the cantonal AFC before activating telework.

item.title: Living in Fenegrò and working in Ticino as a border worker
item.description: Practical guide on taxation, connections and costs for those who choose Fenegrò as a residence working in the Canton of Ticino.
item.content:encoded:
## In breve - Imposta alla fonte trattenuta solo in Svizzera - Nuovo Accordo Frontalieri in vigore dal 1° gennaio 2024 - Franchigia di 10.000 euro per i nuovi frontalieri - Esenzione di 7.500 euro per i vecchi frontalieri (fino al 2033)
## Fatti chiave Accordo Frontalieri: firmato 23/12/2020, vigente dal 01/01/2024 Ratifica Italia: Legge 83 del 13/06/2023 Convenzione doppie imposizioni: 09/12/1976 Franchigia nuovi frontalieri: 10.000 € Esenzione vecchi frontalieri: 7.500 € Trattenuta fiscale: Solo in Svizzera
La scelta di risiedere a Fenegrò per lavorare nel Canton Ticino si inserisce in un quadro normativo preciso, regolato principalmente dal Nuovo Accordo Frontalieri firmato il 23 dicembre 2020 e in vigore dal 1° gennaio 2024. Tale accordo, ratificato in Italia con la Legge 83 del 13 giugno 2023, definisce i parametri fiscali per chi attraversa il confine quotidianamente. La Svizzera, pur non essendo membro UE/SEE, mantiene rapporti stabili con l'Italia basati anche sulla Convenzione per evitare le doppie imposizioni firmata il 9 dicembre 1976.
### Il regime fiscale applicato Per chi lavora in Ticino e risiede a Fenegrò, l'imposta alla fonte sul reddito da lavoro viene trattenuta esclusivamente in Svizzera. L'Italia evita la doppia imposizione attraverso l'applicazione di un credito d'imposta, che il contribuente deve indicare nel quadro CE della dichiarazione dei redditi (modello 730). Questo meccanismo assicura che il carico fiscale sia gestito correttamente tra i due Stati, senza che il lavoratore paghi l'imposta intera in entrambi i paesi.
La gestione delle aliquote fiscali, sia a livello federale che cantonale, è affidata all'Amministrazione Federale delle Contribuzioni (AFC/ESTV) e alle rispettive amministrazioni cantonali. È importante sottolineare che enti come l'Ufficio Federale di Statistica (BFS) o l'UFAS si occupano rispettivamente di rilevazioni dati e previdenza sociale, e non hanno alcun potere nella fissazione delle aliquote fiscali. Per chi desidera analizzare l'impatto di queste trattenute sul proprio stipendio, è possibile utilizzare un [calcolatore](nav:calculator) per stimare il netto mensile. L'analisi della convenienza di vivere a Fenegrò comporta la valutazione di diversi scenari fiscali a seconda della data di inizio dell'attività di frontaliere. Il sistema attuale distingue nettamente tra chi era già frontaliere prima del 17 luglio 2023 e chi ha iniziato successivamente.
### Differenze tra nuovi e vecchi frontalieri I cosiddetti vecchi frontalieri beneficiano di un regime transitorio che copre il periodo 2024–2033, mantenendo un'esenzione fiscale di 7.500 euro. Al contrario, i nuovi frontalieri, ovvero coloro che hanno acquisito lo status dopo la data limite, possono beneficiare di una franchigia di 10.000 euro. Questa distinzione è fondamentale per il calcolo del reddito imponibile in Italia e per l'eventuale determinazione del credito d'imposta.
Dal punto di vista dei contributi sociali, il sistema svizzero prevede trattenute precise che incidono sulla busta paga. I contributi AVS/AI/IPG sono fissati al 5,3% a carico del dipendente, mentre l'assicurazione disoccupazione (AD/AC) assorbe l'1,1%, con un tetto massimo di 148.200 CHF. A questi si aggiunge la LAINF, che varia tra lo 0,7% e l'1,5%, e la previdenza professionale LPP, con aliquote che oscillano tra il 7% e il 18% a seconda della fascia d'età, a partire dai 25 anni.
### Il costo della vita e l'assicurazione sanitaria Risiedere in Italia e lavorare in Svizzera permette di ottimizzare il costo della vita, ma introduce l'obbligo di gestire l'assicurazione malattia (LAMal). I frontalieri con permesso G hanno un diritto d'opzione che permette di scegliere tra il sistema svizzero e quello del paese di residenza. Nel caso in cui si scelga la LAMal, le franchigie per gli adulti variano da 300 a 2.500 CHF. Per confrontare l'incidenza di queste spese rispetto al salario svizzero, si consiglia di consultare i dati sul [costo della vita](nav:cost-of-living) tra Ticino e Italia. Per chi decide di trasferirsi a Fenegrò e iniziare a lavorare in Ticino, è necessario seguire una procedura amministrativa rigorosa per regolarizzare la propria posizione fiscale e previdenziale.
### Step operativi per il frontaliere Il primo passo consiste nell'ottenere il permesso G, il documento che attesta la qualità di lavoratore transfrontaliero. Una volta iniziato l'impiego, il datore di lavoro provvederà alla trattenuta dell'imposta alla fonte, che verrà versata alle autorità fiscali svizzere. Parallelamente, il lavoratore deve monitorare i propri contributi versati all'AVS e alla LPP per la futura pensione.
In Italia, l'Agenzia delle Entrate e il MEF gestiscono la ricezione dei redditi prodotti all'estero. È essenziale che il frontaliere presenti correttamente la dichiarazione dei redditi, utilizzando il quadro CE del modello 730 per richiedere il credito d'imposta e neutralizzare la doppia imposizione, come previsto dalla Convenzione del 1976. Per chi ha dubbi sulla compilazione o sugli importi, è possibile utilizzare un simulatore per la [dichiarazione redditi](nav:tax-return).
### Gestione delle scadenze e degli enti È fondamentale tenere traccia delle comunicazioni provenienti da AFC/ESTV per quanto riguarda le tasse e dall'INPS per l'eventuale coordinamento previdenziale. Se si opta per l'assicurazione sanitaria svizzera, occorre definire la franchigia LAMal entro i termini previsti per evitare sanzioni o coperture limitate.
Per chi è ancora in fase di valutazione del trasferimento, l'analisi del salario lordo rispetto alle trattenute previdenziali e fiscali è il punto di partenza. Calcolare con precisione quanto rimarrà in tasca dopo l'imposta alla fonte e i contributi LPP è l'unico modo per pianificare correttamente il budget familiare a Fenegrò. Per ottenere una stima accurata, suggeriamo di utilizzare il nostro [calcolatore stipendio](nav:calculator).

item.title: Living in Cantù and working in Ticino as a border worker
item.description: Practical guide for those who choose Cantù as their residence: taxation, new border agreement, AVS, LAMal and management of daily commuting to Ticino.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - New Agreement entered into force on January 1, 2024. - Exclusive taxation in Switzerland with a tax credit in Italy. - 10,000 euro tax allowance for new cross-border workers. - Mandatory LAMal insurance for employees with a G permit.
## Key facts Cross-border Workers Agreement: December 23, 2020 Entry into force: January 1, 2024 Allowance for new cross-border workers: 10,000 euro Allowance for existing cross-border workers: 7,500 euro AVS/AI/IPG contribution: 5.3% employee share AD/AC contribution: 1.1% (cap 148,200 CHF)
Moving to Cantù for those working in the Canton of Ticino is a choice that requires careful planning, based on the current regulations governing the relationship between Italy and Switzerland. Since January 1, 2024, the new agreement signed on December 23, 2020, has introduced substantial changes for cross-border workers. Income from employment is taxed exclusively in Switzerland via withholding tax, managed by the cantonal tax administrations and the Federal Tax Administration (AFC/ESTV). To avoid double taxation, the worker must declare the income in Italy, utilizing the tax credit through the CE section of the 730 tax return form.
### Updated tax regulations Workers who were already cross-border commuters before July 17, 2023, benefit from a transitional regime valid until 2033, with a tax exemption of 7,500 euro. For those hired after that date, the allowance is set at 10,000 euro. It is essential to remember that Switzerland is not an EU/EEA member; therefore, the relationship is regulated by the Convention for the avoidance of double taxation signed on December 9, 1976. Swiss social security contributions, such as AVS, AI, and IPG, amount to 5.3% charged to the employee, while unemployment insurance (AD/AC) is 1.1% up to a salary cap of 148,200 francs. The management of these contributions is the responsibility of social security institutions, while tax rates are established by federal and cantonal laws. A cross-border worker residing in Cantù must carefully consider these payroll deductions, which differ significantly from the Italian tax system. Financial planning must also integrate the impact of Italian IRPEF, with brackets at 23%, 35%, and 43% based on total income, applied net of the tax credit recognized for taxes already paid across the border. ### Practical implications of commuting Choosing Cantù means dealing daily with the dynamics of cross-border traffic towards the Canton of Ticino. The main road connection involves using the A9 motorway network, which merges towards the Brogeda border crossing, a nerve center for access into Swiss territory. Managing travel time is a critical factor for those residing far from the immediate border. It is advisable to constantly monitor traffic conditions, as unforeseen events or congestion peaks can heavily influence the quality of work life. From a social security perspective, in addition to the mandatory AVS contributions, the worker must assess their position regarding the second pillar (LPP), with rates varying between 7% and 18% based on age, starting from 25 years old. Managing health insurance coverage is equally crucial: cross-border workers holding a G permit have the right of option for LAMal, the mandatory Swiss health insurance, which provides for deductibles between 300 and 2,500 francs. It is essential not to confuse LAMal with a tax, as it is an insurance coverage necessary to access healthcare services. Compared to the past, the regulatory framework requires greater awareness of income tax declaration procedures. The taxpayer must ensure they correctly document every payment made in Switzerland to maximize the benefit of the tax credit in Italy, thus avoiding excessive taxation. The distinction between withholding tax, managed by the FTA, and social contributions managed by social security institutions, must be clear for every worker. Proper maintenance of tax documentation, keeping copies of Swiss payslips and salary certificates, is the first step for a smooth management of one's status as a cross-border worker residing in Cantù. Family budget planning must include not only transport costs but also currency exchange fluctuations, considering that income is received in Swiss francs.
## Useful tools for your case To verify your within/over 20 km tax scenario, use the [net salary calculator](nav:calculator) and the [tax return guide](nav:tax-return). ### Operational procedures and useful tools For those intending to settle in Cantù and embark on a career path in Ticino, the procedure begins with obtaining the G permit, issued by the competent authorities following a regular employment contract. Subsequently, it is necessary to regularize one's insurance status. The worker must activate LAMal coverage or exercise the right of option, depending on their specific situation, to ensure compliance with current regulations. Regarding social security, it is advisable to monitor one's AVS position and evaluate joining supplementary pension schemes, such as the third pillar, to supplement future income. Managing income requires the use of digital tools to simulate the net salary, considering tax deductions and Swiss social contributions. To effectively compare net income, it is useful to use a [tax calculator](nav:calculator) that allows for estimating the impact of withholding tax and the Italian tax credit. Furthermore, financial planning must take into account commuting costs, including car maintenance expenses and the potential purchase of the Swiss motorway vignette, which is necessary for traveling on Swiss highways. For those wishing to optimize the exchange rate management between CHF and EUR, constant monitoring of exchange rates through a [currency comparator](nav:exchange) is a recommended practice. Finally, for those needing to delve into their health coverage, a [health insurance comparator](nav:health) is available to evaluate the various options offered by LAMal. Transparency and constant updates are the keys to managing one's status as a cross-border worker autonomously and in an informed manner. Any change in income or family situation must be promptly communicated to the competent tax authorities, both in Switzerland and in Italy, to avoid discrepancies in annual declarations. By using the simulation and planning tools provided, the worker can obtain a clear and realistic view of their net income, facilitating prudent and long-term oriented financial management.

item.title: Health insurance premiums: the PLR proposes a cantonal strategy
item.description: The PLR calls for quarterly monitoring of healthcare costs after the 7.1% increase in premiums recorded in Ticino in 2026.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - The FDP proposes a cantonal strategy to curb healthcare costs. - In 2026, health insurance premiums in Ticino rose by 7.1%. - Public spending for RIPAM has increased by 47% in six years. - A quarterly monitoring of healthcare costs in Ticino has been requested.
## Key facts Submission date: September 21, 2026 Proponent: Alessandra Gianella Political group: FDP 2026 premium increase Ticino: 7.1% 2026 premium increase Switzerland: 4.4% 2026 adult premium increase: 6.9% 2026 young adult premium increase: 7.3% 2026 minor premium increase: 7.7%
On September 21, 2026, Alessandra Gianella, on behalf of the FDP group, presented a motion to the Grand Council aimed at implementing a cantonal strategy to contain healthcare spending. The initiative stems from the need to intervene structurally in the costs fueling the growth of health insurance premiums, moving beyond the simple provision of subsidies. The context highlighted by the text is that of a Ticino which recorded an average premium increase of 7.1% in 2026, a figure higher than the 4.4% recorded at the national level. Analyzing the progression by age group, the motion underlines how for adults the increase was 6.9%, for young adults 7.3%, and for minors 7.7%. The projections by bonus.ch mentioned in the document also indicate the possibility of a further national price hike of between 4.5% and 5% for 2027.
### The impact on public coffers The motion emphasizes the financial sustainability of the system, highlighting how the overall expenditure for the Reduction of health insurance premiums (RIPAM) and the coverage of premiums for beneficiaries of OASI/DI supplementary benefits has risen significantly. Specifically, it went from 307.7 million francs in 2020 to 426 million in 2025, with a forecast of 453.5 million for 2026. This increase, equal to about 47% in just six years, raises questions about the stability of the current model. The FDP believes that politics cannot limit itself to transferring the burden of costs from the insured to the taxpayers, highlighting how the middle class is particularly exposed to this dynamic, suffering a contraction of disposable income due to high premiums and the low incidence of individual reduction measures for this category. The analysis proposed by the FDP focuses on the need for more rigorous and transparent healthcare governance within the Canton of Ticino. The motion calls for the introduction of a quarterly, concise, and accessible monitoring of compulsory insurance costs, based on data already available at the federal level. The goal is to break down expenses by major service groups, comparing them with national averages and those of other comparable cantons. In addition to this control tool, an in-depth annual analysis is proposed to identify the causes of expenditure deviations and the sectors where costs are growing most rapidly. Such data should serve as the basis for a cantonal containment strategy, to be updated at least once per legislative period, which defines priorities, measurable objectives, and concrete measures under cantonal jurisdiction.
### Supply planning and EFAS reform A central element of the proposal concerns the planning of healthcare supply, both stationary and outpatient, with the intent of aligning it with the actual needs of the population. The FDP aims to limit redundant capacities and oversupply, which can generate additional costs without providing concrete health benefits. The EFAS reform on the uniform financing of services fits into this framework. The FDP's request is that the Canton prepares for the implementation of the reform not only from a financial perspective, but by favoring the shift of services from the stationary to the outpatient sector, where clinically appropriate. This would improve the overall efficiency of the supply. Furthermore, the motion proposes the establishment of a structured annual dialogue between the main players in Ticino's healthcare system to formulate concrete containment proposals, clearly distinguishing between interventions under cantonal and federal jurisdiction. Regarding transparency, it is requested that every cantonal health policy decision be accompanied by an indication of the expected impact on compulsory insurance costs and that the Government submit a biennial report to the Grand Council on the evolution of expenditure and the results achieved.
## Useful planning tools To estimate your pension strategy, use the [pension planner](nav:pension) and the [pillar 3 simulator](nav:pillar3). For citizens and workers residing or active in Ticino, the issue of rising LAMal premiums represents a primary expense. The FDP motion directly impacts household budgets, which face constant increases and growing indirect fiscal pressure. It is crucial to understand that while the political debate focuses on cost-containment strategies, individual policyholders must continue to actively manage their insurance status. The transparency requested by the motion, if translated into public reports and accessible monitoring, will allow for a clearer view of the factors influencing healthcare spending, facilitating more informed choices. For those working in Ticino, it is essential to constantly monitor price dynamics and available coverage.
### Tools for cost management While waiting for healthcare cost-containment strategies to be implemented, policyholders can utilize established tools to manage their budgets. Choosing the right deductible and regularly reviewing contractual conditions remain the pillars for optimizing the impact of premiums on net income. It is advisable to use official comparison tools to evaluate the various options offered by health insurance funds, keeping in mind that the LAMal system guarantees mandatory coverage but allows for personalized management of risk levels and monthly premiums. For those wishing to delve deeper into the impact of healthcare spending and social charges on their salary, it is essential to use accurate calculation tools. Managing one's payslip, also considering AVS contributions and tax withholdings, requires a clear overview. To verify how different salary components and deductions affect your monthly net income and to better plan the management of your earnings, we invite you to use the [calculator](nav:calculator) dedicated to payslips and taxes.

item.title: Recruitment in the public sector in Ticino: clear rules requested
item.description: Roncelli and Mirante di Avanti with Ticino & Lavoro ask the government about the Zali case and the 2020 email to the ECO.
item.content:encoded:
## In a nutshell - Question by Roncelli and Mirante to the government - Request for clarification on the Zali case and the 2020 email - Focus on EoC recruitment and transparency
## Key facts - Applicants: Roncelli and Mirante (Forward with Ticino & Lavoro) - Episode: Zali case and 2020 email - Entity involved: EOC - Request: Provisions to prevent similar situations
Clear rules are needed to ensure transparency and impartiality in recruitment. This is the central theme raised in the Canton of Ticino by the political representatives Roncelli and Mirante of the Avanti con Ticino & Lavoro movement. The political leaders decided to submit a formal question to the cantonal government to shed light on specific events that have attracted public and institutional attention.
At the centre of the request is the so-called Zali case and a specific email communication dating back to 2020 addressed to the ECO, the Cantonal Hospital Authority. The question aims to understand in detail how the dynamics took place on thatoccasion and what are the administrative implications related to the selection and appointment procedures within the bodies governed by public law or participated in by the Canton.
### The request for institutional clarifications The initiative of the two members of Avanti con Ticino & Lavoro is not limited to retracing the events of the past, but looks directly at the future of cantonal administrative and health management. The issue raised in the public debate closely touches on the delicate balance between political management and the administration of public entities in Ticino Canton. item.title: Inflation in Switzerland: how much does it weigh on budgets?
item.description: Analysis of inflation and purchasing power in Switzerland: find out the distance between the official index and the cost of living lived every day.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - Analysis of inflation and purchasing power in Switzerland - Gap between official inflation and daily experience - The real weight of energy, fuels, and taxes ## Key facts Author: Elio del Biaggio Date: Sep 20, 2026 Update: 19:01
In Switzerland, inflation, price stability, and purchasing power are regularly discussed through figures that, on paper, appear reassuring for citizens and for those who cross the border daily to work in the Canton of Ticino. However, there is a fundamental question that we should have the courage to ask ourselves: whether we are truly measuring everything that heavily impacts family budgets. Between the official inflation reported by statistical indices and the one actually experienced every day at home and on the roads, the gap can prove to be particularly significant. The central core of the issue does not lie in questioning the correctness of the statistics themselves, but rather in understanding what these indicators actually measure and, above all, which fundamental items are deliberately excluded from the reference baskets. When we witness substantial price increases that directly hit primary sectors such as energy, fuels, foodstuffs, housing-related costs, transportation, health insurance premiums, and a wide range of essential services, the cost of daily life grows in a tangible and unmistakable way. ### The hidden pressure on family budgets To the spending on basic necessities are also added taxes, duties, fiscal charges, and further levies that directly or indirectly weigh on final consumer prices, further amplifying the economic pressure on the domestic budgets of residents and cross-border workers. Taking the fuel sector as an example, the price paid at the pump does not depend exclusively on international fluctuations in the cost of oil on global markets, but is largely determined by significant taxation and ancillary charges. Similarly, the cost of energy is not confined to simple car refueling or the domestic electricity bill, but penetrates thoroughly into the price of any good or service that is produced, transported, commercialized, and ultimately purchased and consumed by citizens. Energy is practically present everywhere and inevitably conditions every expense. It is therefore insufficient and misleading to state that overall inflation is contained when, at the same time, a family is forced to allocate an increasingly large share of its income to maintaining the exact same standard of living as before. A purely average index may be impeccable and correct from a strictly statistical point of view, but at the same time prove entirely inadequate and unrepresentative of the actual daily experience lived by a household. Not all consumers purchase the exact same goods, not all face the same structure of fixed and variable costs, and not all suffer with the same intensity from the repercussions of price increases recorded in different economic sectors. For this reason, simply speaking generically about inflation without analyzing the complexity of overall economic pressure can become a misleading exercise that fails to capture the financial reality of taxpayers. ### A statistical snapshot that does not match reality The concrete risk associated with this approach is the construction of a representation of reality that appears artificially reassuring, while the management of everyday household budgets tells a completely different story characterized by greater financial difficulties. An official inflation rate maintained at low levels can easily turn into an untruthful figure when evaluated against the overall perception of the cost of living, especially where all the expense items that heavily impact the economic stability of families are not adequately included and weighted. Addressing this issue requires an approach based on realism and, above all, the utmost intellectual honesty, avoiding sugarcoating an economic situation in which real costs constantly exceed the official estimates published by federal statistical agencies.

Carefully assessing the real impact of inflation on your household budget requires adopting adequate financial planning tools, capable of monitoring the evolution of mandatory and discretionary expenses month after month. For frontier workers and for those who manage entries and exits between Swiss francs and euros, constantly comparing their spending capacity with the real data of the Ticino market is a fundamental measure to avoid unwanted surprises at the end of the year. It is possible to deepen the management of your personal finances, estimate the impact of deductions and verify your economic situation using the [calcolatore](nav:calculator) to better plan the available resources and deal with the cost of living increases with greater awareness.

## In brief - Signed protocol between Confapi Varese and Fondazione AVSI - Objective: train young people through apprenticeship and dual training - Signing took place on September 17 at the Lodovico Pogliaghi House Museum
## Key facts - Signing entity: Confapi Varese - Signing entity: Fondazione AVSI - Signing date: September 17 - Location: Lodovico Pogliaghi House Museum - Parties involved: Marco Tenaglia, Giorgio Capitanio, Roberto Di Francesco
On September 17, in the evocative setting of the Lodovico Pogliaghi House Museum in Santa Maria del Monte, a new memorandum of understanding was signed between Confapi Varese and Fondazione AVSI. The event, part of the benefit evening entitled ‘On the Notes of Varese, Rio and the World’, saw the participation of prominent figures from the two organizations, called upon to formalize a joint commitment aimed at creating a bridge between young people in reception pathways and the productive fabric of small and medium-sized enterprises in the Varese area. The evening was further enriched by the artistic performances of soprano Fernanda Schleder and baritone Frederico de Assis, coming from the Rio de Janeiro Opera Theatre, creating a blend of culture and social purpose.
### Strategic objectives of the protocol The signing of the document, affixed by Marco Tenaglia for Confapi Varese and by Giorgio Capitanio, AVSI Europe Regional Manager, marks the formal start of an operational collaboration. The primary intent is to structure a pathway that combines reception, training and job placement. Fondazione AVSI, leveraging the network of Families for Reception that follows young people in their personal development, will be responsible for identifying profiles ready for the labour market. Confapi Varese, for its part, will deploy its services dedicated to apprenticeship, involving the extensive network of associated small and medium-sized industries. The aim is to effectively meet the professional skill needs of companies, while at the same time offering young people a concrete channel to achieve professional autonomy. This synergy aims to turn corporate social responsibility into an established practice, capable of generating measurable benefits both for companies and for the local Varese community. The agreement fits into an economic landscape in which, according to the source, one out of two companies records serious difficulties in finding the professional figures it needs for its productive activities. The initiative is not limited to a mere programmatic intent, but translates into an operational model based on dual training, which facilitates the insertion of young people into the productive system. The involvement of Api Servizi alle Imprese, in the person of its CEO Roberto Di Francesco, guarantees the provision of specific know-how in training and apprenticeship, essential for building tailor-made paths that respond to the real needs of the small and medium-sized enterprises associated with Confapi.
### Integration and value of work The president of Confapi Varese, Marco Tenaglia, stressed that the ultimate goal is to look to the future, laying the foundations for an authentic and structured integration. The outlined path is based on three fundamental pillars: training, welcome, and cultural value. These components, if correctly integrated, are able to produce tangible benefits both for the young people involved and for the country as a whole. The structure of the agreement provides for a clear distinction of operational competencies: AVSI manages the accompaniment and preparation phase of the young people through its widespread network, while Confapi Varese coordinates the technical phase of job insertion. This systemic approach aims to bridge the gap between the demand for technical skills from companies and the training offer, seeking to make the job insertion process a smooth and well-oiled mechanism capable of enhancing the potential of each young participant in the program. Attention to dual training represents, in this sense, the response to a shortage of professional figures that penalizes not only large industries, but especially the small realities that constitute the economic backbone of the Varese territory.
